title: Billing Dispute Assistant on AWS
context: Northbridge Cloud Distribution wants an assistant that helps its billing agents triage and draft responses to customer invoice disputes. Agents sign in through the corporate identity provider, open a dispute case, and receive a suggested resolution generated by Amazon Bedrock from the case history and uploaded invoices. Confirmed cases are mirrored to the external ticketing system. The workload is a single-Region, single-Availability-Zone deployment sized for about 150 agents.

requirements.text: Agents sign in with the corporate identity provider.
Generate a suggested resolution for each dispute case.
Store cases and invoice attachments encrypted at rest.
Mirror confirmed cases to the external ticketing system.
Single Availability Zone deployment is acceptable for the pilot.

decisions.title: Run services on ECS Fargate
decisions.context: The team is small and does not want to patch or scale container hosts.
decisions.decision: Run the API and the worker as two ECS Fargate services in the private subnet, with images pulled from Amazon ECR.
consequences: Per-task pricing is higher than EC2 at steady high load.

rejected_alternatives.reason: adds host patching and capacity management
cluster operations are out of proportion for two services

decisions.title: Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL for case data
decisions.context: Cases, comments and audit entries are relational and need transactional updates.
decisions.decision: Use one RDS for PostgreSQL 16 instance, db.t4g.medium, gp3 100 GiB, Single-AZ, encrypted with a customer managed KMS key.
consequences: Single-AZ means a failure causes downtime until restore.

rejected_alternatives.reason: cost is higher than needed for the pilot

decisions.title: Generate resolutions with Amazon Bedrock
decisions.context: Suggested resolutions must be produced without hosting a model.
decisions.decision: The worker calls Amazon Bedrock over the Region endpoint, through the NAT Gateway, to draft each resolution.
consequences: Prompts leave the VPC to the Bedrock service endpoint.

decisions.title: Decouple ticket sync with Amazon SQS and Lambda
decisions.context: The external ticketing system is slow and occasionally unavailable.
decisions.decision: The API queues a message in Amazon SQS and an arm64 Lambda function posts it to the ticketing system.

rejected_alternatives.reason: ties agent latency to the external system

components.name: Billing agents
components.purpose: Open and resolve dispute cases from a browser.

components.name: Corporate identity provider
components.purpose: Authenticates agents and issues OIDC tokens.

components.name: Application Load Balancer
components.purpose: Terminates TLS and forwards requests to the API.

components.name: NAT Gateway
components.purpose: Outbound access for private subnet workloads.
components.assumption_reason: Required for private tasks to reach the identity provider and the ticketing system; not stated in the SRS.

components.name: Internet Gateway
components.purpose: Internet path for the public subnet.

components.name: Dispute API service
components.purpose: Serves the agent web API and writes cases to the database.

components.name: Resolution worker service
components.purpose: Builds prompts and calls Amazon Bedrock for suggested resolutions.

components.name: Amazon ECR
components.purpose: Stores the API and worker container images.

components.name: Case Database
components.purpose: Stores cases, comments and audit entries.

components.name: Ticket sync queue
components.purpose: Buffers confirmed cases for the ticketing sync.

components.name: Ticket sync function
components.purpose: Posts queued cases to the external ticketing system.

components.name: AWS Secrets Manager
components.sku_summary: 3 secrets (database, ticketing API key, OIDC client)
components.purpose: Holds database credentials and API keys.

relationships.label: Opens web app
relationships.sentence: Billing agents open the web app through the Application Load Balancer.

relationships.label: Forwards requests
relationships.sentence: The Application Load Balancer forwards requests to the Dispute API service.

relationships.label: Validates tokens
relationships.sentence: The Dispute API service validates sign-in tokens with the Corporate identity provider through the NAT Gateway.

relationships.label: Reads and writes cases
relationships.sentence: The Dispute API service reads and writes cases in the Case Database.

relationships.label: Stores invoices
relationships.sentence: The Dispute API service stores uploaded invoices in the Invoice bucket.

relationships.label: Reads case history
relationships.sentence: The Resolution worker service reads case history from the Case Database.

relationships.label: Requests drafts
relationships.sentence: The Resolution worker service sends prompts to Amazon Bedrock to draft a suggested resolution.

relationships.label: Queues confirmed cases
relationships.sentence: The Dispute API service places each confirmed case on the Ticket sync queue.

relationships.label: Triggers function
relationships.sentence: The Ticket sync queue triggers the Ticket sync function.

relationships.label: Posts tickets
relationships.sentence: The Ticket sync function posts the case to the External ticketing system through the NAT Gateway.

relationships.label: Supplies images
relationships.sentence: Amazon ECR supplies container images to the Dispute API service and the Resolution worker service.

relationships.label: Reads secrets
relationships.sentence: The Dispute API service reads database credentials and API keys from AWS Secrets Manager.

security_operations: RDS, S3 and Secrets Manager are encrypted with the customer managed AWS KMS key.
ECS tasks use separate task roles with least-privilege access to only the resources they call.
The Case Database accepts connections only from the ECS service security groups on port 5432.
Amazon CloudWatch collects service logs with 30-day retention and alarms on task failures and database CPU.

assumptions.text: About 150 billing agents use the system during business hours.
assumptions.reason: The SRS gives the agent population but no usage profile.

assumptions.text: The Corporate identity provider supports OIDC.
assumptions.reason: The SRS says only that sign-in uses the corporate identity provider.

assumptions.text: Invoice attachments are PDF files under 10 MB.
assumptions.reason: Needed to size the Invoice bucket and API limits.

open_questions: Does Northbridge Cloud Distribution require Multi-AZ for the Case Database after the pilot?
Which ticketing system API version must the Ticket sync function target?
